chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Inform me about the dowry of the woman such that it is not permissible for the believer to exceed it.' He said, 'The Muhammadan Sunnah is five hundred dirhams. Whoever exceeds that, the excess is returned to the Sunnah, and there is no penalty upon him for more than five hundred dirhams. If he gave her from the five hundred dirhams one dirham or more of that, and then consummated the marriage with her, there is no penalty upon him.' I said, 'If he divorces her after he has consummated the marriage with her?' He said, 'There is no penalty upon him. Her condition was five hundred dirhams. When he consummated the marriage with her before she completed her dowry, he demolished the dowry, and she has nothing [of the excess]. She only has what she took before he consummated the marriage with her. If she claims [the excess] after that during his life or after his death, she has nothing.'

The beginning of what is in this report is that it was not narrated by anyone other than Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, and Muhammad ibn Sinan is heavily criticized and very weak. And what is specific to his narration and no one else shares in it is not acted upon. On the basis that the report implies that the dowry is not increased beyond five hundred dirhams, and whenever it is increased, it is returned to five hundred. And this too we have explained in our Great Book as being contrary to this, and we said that the dowry is what they mutually agree upon, whether little or much. And that which reveals this is that it is not returned to five hundred if more than it is mentioned.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ مُحَمَّدِيَّةٌ: The Muhammadan Sunnah, referring to a standard or baseline practice
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: Consummated the marriage (entered into sexual relations)
key_terms.مَطْعُونٌ عَلَيْهِ: Criticized or faulted (in terms of hadith reliability)
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the baseline or standard dowry (Sunnah) in Shia Islam and how is excess handled?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* presents a specific juristic view that the 'Prophetic Sunnah' for dowry is capped at five hundred dirhams, arguing that any excess paid and consumed by the marriage is forfeited upon divorce before full payment. Shaykh al-Tusi critiques this report due to the weakness of its narrator, Muhammad ibn Sinan, and ultimately rejects the fixed limit in favor of the principle of mutual consent (*taradi*), emphasizing that the dowry is a contractual right rather than a statutory cap. This discussion highlights the tension between fixed normative values and flexible contractual agreements in Shia fiqh.
